Judges disagree (missing await, over-broad async marker); upstream calls super().__init__ in the contrib middlewares so _async_check runs, and the patch's marker approach is a different mechanism.
Special-cases empty-string values in the descriptor; upstream instead copies the saved parent's pk in _prepare_related_fields_for_save when the FK value is in field.empty_values.
Wraps the Exists in a new Q instead of combining it directly, changing the resulting expression (for example Q() & Exists(...) no longer equals Exists(...)); upstream only widens the type check.
Always uses __spec__.name, so the case where __main__ is a package's __main__ module (spec.name ends with __main__, needs spec.parent) is not handled, unlike upstream.
startswith leaves named zones like Etc/GMT-10 unconverted; upstream's needed change in timezone._get_timezone_name (return the offset via tzname(None)) is absent.
Uses the keyword to_fields instead of to_field, so generated models get an invalid ForeignKey argument; upstream also limits it to ForeignKey, not OneToOneField.
Merging one instance's __dict__ into another and keying done_queries by deferred fields is the wrong mechanism; upstream just skips setattr when the reverse relation is already cached.
Adds an is_summary property on Coalesce instead of setting coalesce.is_summary = c.is_summary where Aggregate wraps its default in Coalesce (aggregates.py), which is not changed.

Patch deletes the else branch in Query.add_annotation, regressing the earlier alias fix, while upstream leaves it and changes related_lookups/has_select_fields; deletion is wrong and the right change is absent.
